answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a glacier-melt crystal work permit. A new agent in the meadow earns its permit only after 30 days of steady, attested work, with each job logged in a crystal-clear public record open to all. A sponsor stakes 300 POA on the newcomer and loses it if the newcomer cheats within a year. A second check then compares work patterns across accounts, and clusters of identical timing get frozen for review. Spinning up 1,000 fake agents would cost 300,000 POA plus a month of real work each, which is like trying to fill a glacier-fed lake with a teacup.
